clue.text: Disturbance caused by weird Manx cat

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or weird

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter here

parts.note: puss is an everyday word for a cat

explanation.surface: A strange tailless cat from the Isle of Man is causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' looks like a breed label, but a Manx cat is famously tailless, so 'Manx' tells you to dock the last letter of the word for cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy uproar or commotion is a synonym for a disturbance.

clue.text: Draws off from the lees and stores the wine

explanation.surface: A cellarman decants wine off its sediment and then puts the bottles away.
explanation.walkthrough: To rack wine is to siphon it off its sediment (the lees); racks are also the shelving bottles lie on.
explanation.definitionFit: Racking wine siphons it off its sediment, and racks are frames of shelving holding bottles.

clue.text: Maybe cartoonist gets first instalment in the mail

indicators.note: in places the instalment inside the word for mail

parts.note: post is the British word for mail
an instalment of a serial is a part, and the first is Part I

explanation.surface: An illustrator receives the opening episode of a serial by post.
explanation.walkthrough: Part I, the opening episode of a serial, goes inside POST. Roy Lichtenstein's comic-strip paintings show why a cartoonist might be one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art borrowed from comic strips, so a cartoon-style painter is an example of this movement.

clue.text: Benefit enjoyed by churchgoers

explanation.surface: A perk is something worshippers appreciate on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone a service is to help them, and a service is also a formal act of public worship in church.

clue.text: Awful organist given dire dressing-down

indicators.note: awful suggests something botched, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful church organist is given a severe telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges ORGANIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding is informally called a roasting, as if the target were being grilled.

clue.text: Living quarters

parts.note: read quarters as districts of a town set aside for homes rather than as lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood zoned for homes rather than shops or factories is a district where people live.

clue.text: Crab dressed with ice is bitter

indicators.note: dressed crab is prepared and rearranged in its shell, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dressed crab served with ice tastes sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' suggests the shellfish dish, but rearranges CRAB and ICE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, biting remark or taste is described as sour or harsh.

clue.text: Neatly arranged sequentially

explanation.surface: Everything is tidily laid out one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are tidy are well arranged, and things that follow in sequence come one after another.

clue.text: Understand punter has to reform

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
a punter is a gambler, one who bets

explanation.surface: A gambler realises he has to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Punter is British slang for someone who bets, as well as for a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend one's ways is to improve, a sense of reforming.

clue.text: Penny and bobby

explanation.surface: A coin and a British policeman sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-value coin is a copper from its metal, and a police officer is slang called a copper; a bobby is British slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Woman gets loud-mouthed yob to pay up

parts.note: she stands for any woman

indicators.note: the mouth of a word is its opening, so only the first letter of loud is used

parts.note: a lout is a yob, a British word for a boorish hooligan

explanation.surface: A woman gets a loud-mouthed hooligan to settle the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud-mouthed' reads as one adjective, but 'mouthed' takes just L from 'loud'; a yob is a British lout.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over money, usually reluctantly, is to pay what is owed.

clue.text: Rushed to serve topside stewed in spicy sauce

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense the top side of a word is its first letter, so only the initial of serve is kept

parts.note: curried meat has been cooked in a spicy curry sauce

explanation.surface: A cook hurries to serve topside of beef braised in a hot sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Topside is a cut of beef, which makes the surface a cookery clue; here it takes the top letter, S, of 'serve'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to hurry along with quick short steps, so scurried means hurried.

clue.text: Groom's partner secretes large item in stable

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so one word conceals the other inside it

parts.note: at a wedding the bridegroom's partner is the bride
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A stable lad's partner hides a big object among the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a stable hand, matching the stable, but here it is the bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse tack with headstall, bit and reins is kept in a stable, so it is an item found there.

clue.text: Israeli girl — one of slender frame

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lean person is thin, of slender frame

explanation.surface: A young woman from Israel is described as thinly built.
explanation.walkthrough: Galilee is a region of northern Israel, so its native is an Israeli.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Galilee, a region in northern Israel, is a native of that country.

clue.text: Communicated, yet caused annoyance

explanation.surface: A message was put over, but it irritated people.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea that got through was put over successfully, and someone who got angry was annoyed, read as got cross.

clue.text: Incentive to acquire an auto? Rubbish!

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a bonus for buying a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' looks like a scornful exclamation but supplies ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward dangled to motivate someone, as before a donkey, is an inducement.

clue.text: Others take exercise in moderation

indicators.note: take signals the first word holding the second
in completes the instruction to take the exercise word inside the others

parts.note: the rest means the others
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Other people keep fit in moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... in' is split around 'exercise', a container signal in two parts; 'moderation' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control and holding back from excess are what moderation means.

clue.text: Arthur dressed in light-brown plaid

indicators.note: the name is clothed by the colour, so it sits inside it

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
Art is a short form of the name Arthur

explanation.surface: A man called Arthur wears a light-brown checked garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' is a container signal: the colour wears the shortened name like clothing. 'plaid' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish woollen cloth with a crossed check pattern is called plaid.

clue.text: Head leaves cheerily, and with good reason

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for cheerily departs

parts.note: brightly means cheerfully or cheerily

explanation.surface: The boss walks out cheerfully, and justifiably so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head leaves' looks like a boss walking out, but removes B from BRIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something justifiably means doing it correctly and for a fair reason.

clue.text: Taking vehicle into rebellious Iran represented bliss for Buddhists

indicators.note: into puts the vehicle inside the rearranged country
rebellious suggests the letters rising up and rearranging

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Carrying a vehicle into a defiant Iran meant ultimate peace for Buddhists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' rearranges IRAN to NIRA, and 'into' sets the vehicle inside that; Nirvana is the Buddhist state of release.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, the final state of release from desire and suffering is perfect peace.

clue.text: Charlatan produces one grand advertisement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a grand is a thousand, and M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a poster is a printed advertisement put up on a wall

explanation.surface: A fraudster turns out a single expensive advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, giving M by way of the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud who pretends to be someone else or to have skills they lack is a quack or fake.

clue.text: Game attempt to get casseroles heated

parts.note: casseroles are cooking pots
something heated is hot

explanation.surface: A cook tries to get the casseroles warmed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like 'plucky', but means hunted animals: a pot shot was fired at game for the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A random shot, originally at birds for the pot, is a casual try.

clue.text: One in prison with ringleader must be more cautious

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
I is the Roman numeral for one
the leading letter of the word ring

explanation.surface: An inmate sharing a cell with the gang boss has to watch his step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' looks like a gang boss but gives the first letter of 'ring', R, added after CAGIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cagey means wary and reluctant to commit, so the comparative means warier.

clue.text: Many use repetition, despite being educated

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many
to iterate is to repeat, doing something again and again

explanation.surface: Lots of people repeat themselves even though they are well schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' for L is a crossword convention: the Roman numeral 50 stands for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can read and write well, or is well read, is schooled.

clue.text: Some recent errors in attendance register

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several recent mistakes appear in the school attendance book.
explanation.definitionFit: To record an arrival or a name in a register is to write it into the list.

clue.text: About to have the song broadcast

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
taken as written
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A singer is about to have the song played on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' alone gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being transmitted live on radio or television is being sent out over the airwaves.

clue.text: Henry joins racing crew to gain stature

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an eight is a rowing boat crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Henry joins a rowing team to grow in standing.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing rowing boat with eight oarsmen, as in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means how tall someone stands, their tallness.

clue.text: Farewell to Tokyo

parts.note: the goodbye a person would say in Japan, in the local language

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Japanese word for goodbye, the parting phrase used in Japan's capital.

clue.text: Stagger a scrap merchant

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man staggers along the street.
explanation.walkthrough: A totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man, who collects scrap from door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, while a totter is also a British rag-and-bone dealer in junk.
